description: issue #681 (slice I2), the observable half of the BLOCKING property: `spec/interaction-events.md:156-159` — while `input` is waiting the implementation "MUST NOT run new OpenLogo instructions or event handler blocks until the read finishes or the program is cancelled." A key `a` is pending from tick 0 and an `on_key "a"` handler is registered, yet the read delivers nothing: the stream contains the handler REGISTRATION `primitive`, the read's own `primitive`, and the final `print` of the answer — no `handler ran`. Its control twin `input-blocking-control-wait-delivers` runs the identical program with `wait 0` in the reading position and the SAME pending key, and there the handler DOES fire; the pair is what makes this an assertion rather than a vacuous absence. A fixture cannot prove the property in full — with a scripted answer the read returns immediately, so there is no waiting interval a headless fold can observe — so the complete proof, including that a read never advances the tick clock (no `every` can come due), lives in `packages/runtime/src/interaction-input-blocking.test.mjs`.
